item.title: Shrinkwrap 0.39.0
item.description:
Fixed

  • A scan that carries its scanner's own colour profile is now processed. Before, it failed in every format with "encode failed" and nothing was made from it. Only @email worked. The scan's colours are kept and the image is written in Display P3.
  • A floating point TIFF, as Photoshop's 32-bit mode and HDR tools save, is now processed. Before, every such file failed in every format with "encode failed" and nothing was made from it. Only @email worked. The image is written in the colour space the file is in, exactly as a 16-bit TIFF of the same picture is: an sRGB one stays sRGB, a Rec. 2020 one stays Rec. 2020, and a linear one becomes the standard version of its space. Highlights brighter than white are written as white.
  • An image saved in a linear colour space, as 3D renderers and HDR tools export, keeps its shadow detail. Before, dark areas came out in visible bands in every format except @email. The image is now written in the standard version of the same colour space, so linear sRGB becomes sRGB and linear Display P3 becomes Display P3, and its colours do not change.
  • Images made from an SVG keep its exact colours and are smaller. Before, each one carried a colour profile it did not need, which made a favicon several times larger than it had to be, and semi-transparent shapes and soft edges came out slightly off colour.
  • A JPEG made from a picture with a large colour profile, such as a scan or a picture saved in a printer's profile, now carries that profile and keeps its colours. Before, the profile was left out of the JPEG, so its colours could come out visibly wrong in every app. JPEGs saved at quality 100 were not affected.
  • @nobg keeps the colours of a wide-gamut image, such as one in Display P3. Before, removing the background also converted the image to sRGB, which dulled its most saturated colours.
  • A JPEG that describes its colours with numbers in its EXIF data, and has no colour profile, now comes out in the colours Preview shows for it. Before, its colours could come out different from the original. If the numbers made no sense, the image came out completely black, and that could also happen with a TIFF.
  • PNGs come out much smaller on a Mac without the optional pngquant tool, which is almost every Mac. A flat graphic such as an email banner is now about a third of its original size. Before, the same banner could come out larger than the file you started with. On these Macs the quality setting now also changes how small a PNG gets, as it does for other formats.
  • A small PNG that carries a colour profile, such as an icon made from a Display P3 image, no longer comes out larger than it has to. Before, Shrinkwrap could keep the reduced-colour version of the image even when the full-colour version was the smaller file.
  • A PNG that cannot be made smaller is no longer written larger than the original. When nothing about the picture was changed, Shrinkwrap keeps the image data the file came with and removes only its metadata.
  • A wide-gamut PNG that Shrinkwrap has already compressed, such as one in Display P3, keeps its colours when it is processed again. Before, its most saturated colours came out duller the second time and its colour profile was dropped. The same is fixed for any wide-gamut PNG or TIFF that stores its colours as a palette, such as an indexed export from a design tool.
  • Flat colours in a compressed PNG now keep their exact values. Before, a flat background could come out speckled.
  • A WebP or lossless PNG made from a picture in Adobe RGB or ProPhoto RGB now carries the colour profile the picture came with, and is the same file every time it is made. Before, the profile was replaced by a copy stamped with the time, so the file came out slightly different each time. Colours are unchanged.
  • An image made from a picture that describes its colours with numbers and no colour profile, such as an older PNG with a gamma value, is now the same file whenever it is made. Before, the profile written for it was stamped with the date, so the file came out different from one day to the next. Colours are unchanged.
  • The transparent area around a soft shadow or glow stays fully transparent, and solid areas stay fully solid. Before, either could come out very slightly off.
  • Many JPEGs and WebPs that are already heavily compressed are no longer written larger than the original. Before, saving one at a higher quality than it was made with could nearly double its size. When nothing about the picture was changed and saving it again would not make the file smaller, Shrinkwrap keeps the picture data the file came with and removes only its metadata. Copyright and credit are kept as before. For now this covers a JPEG or WebP whose width and height are both multiples of 16 pixels, and some JPEGs at multiples of 8. Pictures of other sizes, a WebP with transparency, and AVIF and HEIC files are still saved again as before and can still come out larger.
  • A JPEG that keeps its copyright or credit is now compressed once, at the quality you asked for. Before, the picture was compressed and then, to add those fields, compressed a second time by macOS at a quality of its own. At the default quality that made the file one and a half to two times as large as it should have been, and at any quality it cost a little detail. Now the fields are added without touching the picture, so the image is exactly the one you get with @strip, with the fields added. This includes large pictures in an HDR colour space, which macOS handles differently from the rest. Images made before this update stay as they are.
  • A PNG that keeps its copyright or credit is now compressed as well as any other PNG. Before, Shrinkwrap did not reduce the colours of such a PNG, because the step that does that cannot write those fields. A photo with nothing more than a photographer's name in it came out three to four times the size of the same photo without one. Now the fields are added after the colours are reduced, without touching the picture, so the image is exactly the one you get with @strip, with the fields added. A name costs about 550 bytes. Two kinds of picture that keep such a field are still saved without reducing their colours: a very small one, where that is the smaller file, and one in an HDR colour space. Images made before this update stay as they are.
  • A favicon or web clip no longer carries the copyright and credit of the picture it was made from. Those fields were larger than a 16 pixel icon itself, and a favicon.ico held them twice.
  • A PNG made from an HDR picture, such as a 10-bit HEIC or AVIF, now keeps its colours. Before, Shrinkwrap reduced the colours of such a PNG as it does for any other, and Preview, Quick Look and Safari then showed it lighter or darker than the original and without its HDR highlights. These PNGs are now saved without reducing their colours. They are three to four times larger and look like the picture they came from. Ordinary pictures are not affected. Images made before this update stay as they are.
  • A PNG is no longer shown turned because of the wording of its copyright or credit. If one of those fields held the text tiff:Orientation followed by a digit from 2 to 8, Safari and Quick Look showed the PNG that Shrinkwrap made turned or flipped, and Shrinkwrap did too if that PNG was used as a source. Now Shrinkwrap writes one character of that text in a different form inside the PNG, which reads back as exactly the same words and no longer turns the picture. JPEG, WebP, AVIF and HEIC never had this problem. Images made before this update stay as they are.
  • A JPEG or WebP whose artist is stored only in a short EXIF block, one with no camera make or model, orientation or resolution in it, now keeps that name. macOS reports the artist of such a file in a different place from the usual one and Shrinkwrap did not look there, so the name was left out of everything made from the picture. Photos straight from a camera were not affected. Add @strip to leave the name out.
  • A copyright, credit or source longer than 2,000 bytes is now kept only up to that length. A list of bylines or artists is kept up to 2,000 bytes and 32 names, and is cut between names and not inside one, unless the first name alone is too long. The log says which fields were shortened. Before, a field longer than about 64,000 bytes made the JPEG Shrinkwrap wrote unreadable in some apps.
  • A copyright, artist, credit, byline or source that holds nothing but spaces no longer counts as a credit. Shrinkwrap kept such blanks, so a PNG made from a photo that had them was saved without reducing its colours and came out much larger than it should have, and every JPEG carried the empty fields. Such a photo is now treated like any other photo with no credit.
  • A JPEG that keeps both a credit and a source is now the same file every time it is made, where the macOS encoder writes it. That includes every JPEG made with @lossless or @q100, and an HDR picture of about three megapixels or more at any quality. Shrinkwrap handed the encoder those fields in an order that changed from one time to the next, so the same picture could come out as up to four slightly different files, each with the same picture and the same fields. Two Macs sharing a synced folder could each write a different one and leave a conflicted copy. JPEGs that Shrinkwrap's own encoder writes, and PNG, WebP, AVIF and HEIC files, did not have this problem.
  • A PNG that is saved rotated and also carries details such as a copyright is now turned and sized the way the file says to show it. Before, Shrinkwrap measured such a PNG as rotated but wrote it unrotated, so a width or height you asked for was applied to the wrong side, the result could be much smaller than it needed to be, and the size in its file name could be wrong. Chrome shows these PNGs rotated. Quick Look and web views built on WebKit currently show them unrotated, so there the result looks rotated compared with the original.

item.title: Shrinkwrap 0.38.0 Beta
item.description:
This is a beta. You are getting it because Get beta updates is on in Shrinkwrap Settings.

Fixed

  • Two Macs that share a synced folder, such as one in Dropbox, no longer process the same change at the same moment and leave conflicted copies. They now take turns. The Mac you are using goes first. A Mac nobody is using waits up to a minute and then finds the work already done. When you move to your other Mac, its first change can take 10 to 20 seconds longer. This needs the update on both Macs. Until then the updated Mac waits for the other one.
  • A copy of a result, such as a conflicted copy made by Dropbox, is no longer treated as a new image and compressed a second time. If your Mac made the extra conflicted copy, Shrinkwrap moves it to z_originals/_leftovers.

item.title: Shrinkwrap 0.37.0 Beta
item.description:
This is a beta. You are getting it because Get beta updates is on in Shrinkwrap Settings.

Added

  • Sign Out All Macs in Settings > Account signs every Mac out of your account, including the one you are using, and frees every place on your membership. Use it when a Mac was sold or lost while still signed in, then sign in again on the Macs you keep.

Changed

  • A Mac that was signed out from another Mac now says so the next time its Account settings open, and no longer shows the membership as if it were still signed in.

item.title: Shrinkwrap 0.36.0
item.description:
Added

  • Settings > Account now lists the Macs on your membership. Sold or replaced a Mac? Remove it there and its place is free for your new one. A Mac that signed in while every place was taken can be added as soon as one frees up.

Changed

  • Settings and the welcome tour now match the menu bar search. They share its translucent surface and warm glow, and the Settings tabs have icons and light up under the pointer.
  • Uninstall now sits at the bottom of the Account tab in Settings.
  • The sign-in option for product emails now reads Email me about new features.
  • Signing out now frees that Mac's place on your membership.

Fixed

  • Signing out on one Mac no longer ends your session on your other Macs.
  • The welcome tour now says where originals go. Folders file them in z_originals, and a single image tagged on its own goes to the Trash.

item.title: Shrinkwrap 0.34.0
item.description:
Added

  • Settings has a new Get beta updates switch. Turn it on to get new features before everyone else. Turning it off keeps your current version until a newer regular release comes out.

item.title: Shrinkwrap 0.33.0
item.description:
Added

  • Shrinkwrap has its own app icon: the yellow @ tile from the welcome screen.

item.title: Shrinkwrap 0.32.0
item.description:
Added

  • @color now works as another way to write @recolor, as in @color-white or @color-ff3366. @colour works too. Custom macro names can no longer start with color- or colour-.
  • Colour tags such as @recolor and @bg now take every CSS colour name, like gold, slategray or rebeccapurple. In the menu bar search, start typing a colour and press Tab to finish its name.
  • British spellings work throughout: @fill-centre and @crop-centre are the same as @fill-center, including after a size, as in @800sqfill-centre.

Changed

  • Clicking the menu bar icon now opens a tag search. Start typing to find a tag, choose one with the arrow keys and Return or with a click, and it is copied to the clipboard. A tag that needs a value, such as @recolor, asks for it first: type a colour and press Return. You can also type the value straight into the search, as in "recolor navy". Below the search are any warnings, folders with errors, pause and resume, your stats, your account, Settings and Check for Updates.
  • Process Folder has moved to Settings, under Watched Folders. New Tagged Folder is still in Finder's right-click menu and on the keyboard shortcut.

item.title: Shrinkwrap 0.31.0
item.description:
Added

  • @recolor turns every visible pixel one colour, keeping transparency and smooth edges. Use a colour name or hex, such as @recolor-white, @recolor-black or @recolor-ff3366. A logo made of flat colours becomes one solid colour. Artwork with a gradient or shading keeps its light and dark as shades of the new colour. Add -flat or -shaded, as in @recolor-white-flat, to choose for yourself. It works on folders and single files, and with @favicon and @webclip. SVGs are recoloured when converted, so pair them with @png.

item.title: Shrinkwrap 0.30.0
item.description: New: if a tagged file or @ folder can't run because its name includes a tag Shrinkwrap doesn't know, such as @2x in "photo @png@2x.png", the menu bar icon now shows a warning badge. Click it to see the name and the tag that's wrong, then clear it. Renaming the file clears it too. shrinkwrap parse and the run log now name the unknown tag as well.

item.title: Shrinkwrap 0.29.0
item.description: New: Macs that share a synced folder, such as Dropbox, now take turns on it. The Mac working in a folder marks it busy and the others wait; if that Mac quits or sleeps, another takes over within a few minutes. Shrinkwrap no longer rewrites a file with the bytes already there, so sync stays quiet. Fixed: folder colours could flip back and forth between Macs. Fixed: another Mac could move outputs to _leftovers while their original was still syncing in. Fixed: another Mac could redo or trash a lone tagged image that was already handled, including one restored with Put Back. New custom macro names one letter away from a built-in tag, such as @crops, are now refused; macros you already have keep working. Fixed: shrinkwrap selftest put test images in your Trash.

item.title: Shrinkwrap 0.28.0
item.description: New: Shrinkwrap membership. Subscribe from Settings for $8 a month or $49 a year, and manage billing from the same place. New: change the tags on an image you already replaced. Shrinkwrap keeps the original on your Mac (5 GB by default, adjustable in Settings, or Forever) and renders the new version from it instead of the compressed copy. Account and processing settings are reorganized.

item.title: Shrinkwrap 0.27.0
item.description: New: custom macros. Create your own @tags in Settings, with alternate spellings, and edit, delete or undo them. When a folder can't meet its @max size, Shrinkwrap now asks once per run instead of once per image. Excluded files are skipped before any other tag is read. Account and sign-in screens no longer show the old one-time prices. Fixed: an image dropped both inside and beside an @ folder produced every output twice. Fixed: changing a folder's format gave its old outputs a doubled size stamp when they were moved to _leftovers.

item.title: Shrinkwrap 0.26.0
item.description: The app now ships its own JPEG and WebP encoders (mozjpeg, libwebp) and a built-in PNG quantizer, so every install gets the small files Homebrew users had. @email renders for the worst client in the room: 1200 px wide, JPEG unless transparent, sRGB, metadata stripped, capped at 1 MB, and a note when Outlook would cut it off. Display P3 JPEGs keep their colour.
